findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed that the handwashing sinks in the bathrooms are not fully sealed to the wall. PICs were notified, and will get the sinks fully sealed to the walls to ensure that they are smooth, easily cleanable, and preventing any potential for seepage or spillage.
findings.citation_text: 4-402.11(A) Fixed Equipment, Spacing or Sealing. (A) EQUIPMENT that is fixed because it is not EASILY MOVABLE shall be installed so that it is: (1) Spaced to allow access for cleaning along the sides, behind, and above the EQUIPMENT; (2) Spaced from adjoining EQUIPMENT, walls, and ceilings a distance of not more than 1 millimeter or one thirty-second inch; or (3) SEALED to adjoining EQUIPMENT or walls, if the EQUIPMENT is exposed to spillage or seepage. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed the facility did not have test strips during the inspection. An employee purchased quat test strips and returned with them during the inspection. These test strips must remain at the facility and be used frequently. Ensure there are always test strips available to measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions (quat = 200-400 ppm).

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
During the routine inspection today, inspector observed several priority/priority foundation violations which have been allowed to occur and remain out of compliance. The person-in-charge of the facility is responsible for ensuring that NO priority violations are allowed to occur. Active managerial control is lacking based upon the discussion with the operator who instructed items to be corrected but no corrective actions were taken by staff. A follow-up is issued for 12/26/2023 to check on compliance with all priority/priority foundation violations AND active managerial control relating to food service operations. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand sinks in the bathroom and in the kitchen were observed to be without paper towels during the inspection today. Hand sinks must be properly stocked with paper towels and hand soap at all times. Ensure that all designated hand sinks are stocked as required. A follow-up is being issued for 01/13/2024 during a scheduled event for 7:30 PM with food preparation starting at 5:30 PM. SCDPH supervisor has approved the off-hours reinspection.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
A failed cooler/freezer full of foods was observed in the facility. Foods in the cooling unit are rotting and odorous. These foods are not safe for consumption nor safe to be stored in the facility. Ensure that foods are removed immediately. A follow-up is issued for 01/03/2024 to ensure that foods have been removed. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Visibly contaminated foods are observed in the failed cooler. These foods pose a serious threat to the safety of other foods and surfaces within the facility and must be discarded immediately. Foods in the upright cooler in large, establishment owned containers which appear to be used for service are stored underneath personal drinks and foods including open, partially consumed alcoholic beverages. Foods prepared in the facility must be protected from contamination at all times. Ensure that foods are properly stored. If personal foods are to be stored, they must be located in an area clearly identified as an area for personal storage. A follow-up is issued for 01/03/2024 to ensure compliance with food storage requirements. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Nearly all food-contact surfaces throughout the facility appear to be soiled as of the inspection today. Inspector observed pans, baking sheets, waffle makers, and other food contact surfaces visibly soiled with aged food residue and debris. Additionally, the food-contact surfaces of the ice machine including all ice bin walls, the freezing tray and water outlet are visibly contaminated with mold. These surfaces must ALL be cleaned and sanitized before use. All ice in the ice bin must be discarded and not used for service. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up is issued for 01/03/2024 to ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized properly and at appropriate frequencies. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper disposition of returned, previously served, reconditioned and unsafe food
findings.comment:
Per conversation with operator, the condition of foods within the failed cold cooler/freezer was known in advance of the inspection performed today. Although several conversations were held with staff regarding discarding the food items stored inside, foods were not discarded. Per 2017 FDA Code, all foods which are contaminated by any means including mishandling must be discarded. Ensure that foods are discarded when unsafe for consumption. A follow-up is issued for 01/03/2024 to ensure that all foods stored within the facility are safe and unsafe foods are immediately discarded and not offered for service. 

3-701.11: (A) FOOD unsafe, ADULTERATED, or not honestly presented shall be discarded or reconditioned. (B) FOOD not from APPROVED source shall be discarded. (C) RTE FOOD that may have been contaminated from RESTRICTED/EXCLUDED employee shall be discarded. (D) FOOD contaminated by hands, bodily discharges, or other means shall be discarded.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
TCS foods stored in the failed cooler and remaining in the cooler are stored at between 60 and 70 degrees F. All TCS foods must be stored below 41 degrees F and monitored regularly. Ensure that cold-holding temperatures in all coolers containing food are maintained below 41 degrees F. A follow-up is issued for 01/03/2024 to ensure compliance with cold holding requirements. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
No date marking was observed throughout the facility during the inspection today. Several prepared foods in both refrigerators were observed to lack date marking as required. All foods prepared within the facility must be properly marked with the date prepared/date to be discarded to ensure that foods are discarded within the 7-day period following preparation. A follow-up is issued for 01/13/2024 to ensure that date marking is properly completed on all foods requiring such date marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
A soiled, previously wet wiping cloth was observed sitting on the center counter of the kitchen on arrival. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer between used AND once soiled must be properly laundered. Wet wiping cloths may never be stored on counters. Ensure that all wiping cloths are stored properly.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the ice scoop to be stored on top of the ice machine which was visibly soiled with food residue. In-use utensils must be stored in cleaned and sanitized locations. Ensure that all utensils are stored properly. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Several nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment including but not limited to the stove, oven, waffle makers, and sinks are observed to be soiled with food residue and debris. All nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment must be cleaned at a frequency which prevents any accumulation of residue and debris. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned at the proper frequency.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Waste water from the operations of the facility must be appropriately disposed of once generated. Inspector observed heavily soiled mop water in a mop bucket in the kitchen which has been left for several days. A sanitizer container on the counter with wiping cloths was observed to contain soiled water which had been left for several days. Additionally, inspector observed multiple containers full of soiled water in warewashing sinks which were used for soaking items. Soiled water must IMMEDIATELY be discarded and not allowed to sit in the facility. Ensure that all waste water is appropriately removed from the facility immediately. A follow-up is issued for 01/03/2024 to ensure that all waste water has been removed. 

5-402.13: SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Base coving in the bathroom is missing along the north and east walls. The floor/wall junctures are soiled with water and other residue and debris. As such, these areas are required to be SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE at all times. Ensure that the base coving is replaced.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
